cards.explanation: The answer is that the disciples rebuke the people. When the disciples saw the babies coming, they rebuked those who brought them (Luke 18:15). The text doesn't say why, so I'm not going to guess for them. I think those folks hoped for a warm welcome and got a stern word instead. Bringing a baby to Jesus and hearing a rebuke is a rough turn.

The answer is True, and Jesus says it plainly: “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.” He calls the children to Him first, and then He speaks. That's a welcome with the door held wide open, friends.

The answer is like a little child. Jesus says, “Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.” He says it right after He welcomes the children. Sometimes I think the lesson is in how a little one receives, and I'm still learning it myself. I've got a mustache full of flour and a lot to learn.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “No one is good except God alone.” He answers with a question first: “Why do you call Me good?” I won't guess what's behind it, because the text doesn't say. It just tells us what He says, and that's plenty to chew on.

The answer is False. The ruler answers, “All these I have kept from my youth…” That's his whole reply to the list of commandments. No confession of any slip-ups, just that he has kept them since he was young.

The answer is treasure in heaven. Jesus says, “Sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven.” Notice He tells the ruler what he will have, not only what he gives up. I got bought for 25 cents at a bakery that was closing, and I can tell you treasure in heaven beats that any day.

The answer is to come and follow Him. Jesus says, “Then come, follow Me.” Look at the order, friends. First the selling and giving, then the following. The invitation to follow is the last thing He says to the ruler.

The answer is that he becomes very sad. When the ruler heard it, he became very sad. I think this part hurts a little. The ruler asked a real question and got a real answer. Verse 24 says Jesus saw his sadness.

The answer is wealthy. Verse 23 says the ruler became very sad because he was extremely wealthy. That's the reason the text gives, so we can say it with confidence. I'll leave the rest of his heart to God.

The answer is a camel passing through the eye of a needle. Jesus says, “Indeed, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.” A camel is a big animal and a needle's eye is a tiny hole. That picture gets the point across fast, and nobody needs a diagram.

The answer is True. Those who heard Jesus asked, “Who then can be saved?” It's a fair question after the camel and the needle. I think they were stunned. That's my guess, because the text just gives us the question.

The answer is God. Jesus says, “What is impossible with man is possible with God.” That's His answer to the question about who can be saved. I know what it's like to think a thing is over for good, because I spent years in the back of a junk drawer. Then God reached in and called me out.
The answer is all they had. Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, says, “Look, we have left all we had to follow You.” He says all, not a little. He's telling Jesus the whole of it.

The answer is False. Jesus says anyone who has left home or family for the sake of the kingdom of God will receive many times more in this age. Then He adds that in the age to come, they will receive eternal life. So it's not all saved up for later, friends.

The answer is eternal life. Jesus says that in the age to come, they will receive eternal life. That's the big one. Notice He gives them something in this age too, but eternal life is what He names for the age to come.
